key_insight: Detonation spraying parameters strongly control the trade-off between coating density, friction, wear resistance, and hardness in self-fluxing Ni–Cr–Fe–B–Si–C coatings.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing barrel filling, gas ratio, and inter-shot delay can improve coating performance for restoration and surface strengthening of machine components.
method: Changed inter-shot delay from 0 to 1 s and evaluated coating microstructure, roughness, hardness, friction, and wear.
evidence_signal: The best friction performance occurred at 48% filling and O/C = 1.026 (μ = 0.674 ± 0.136), while the best wear resistance was achieved at O/C = 1.856 with 1 s delay, reducing specific wear rate to 0.000189 mm³/(N·m).
watch_item: Lower friction conditions increased wear, so the process must be tuned carefully to avoid sacrificing durability for low drag.
paper_title: Development of a Method for Producing Self-Fluxing Nickel-Based Coatings by Detonation Spraying
